card.title: The Initiated One
card.instruction: Treat others as recent initiates, revealing rules and information in carefully measured doses that preserve your seniority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first shift on the club door. I'll teach you half the secret handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't I need the whole thing to admit people?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can greet them. I'll handle admission until you've progressed to the wrist.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The president wants me to train tomorrow's doorman.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Teach him the fingers. I'll teach you the wrist while he waits outside.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 teaches only half the handshake, A3 reserves wrist knowledge and admission, and A5 keeps the new trainer one lesson ahead of the next recruit but below A.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's admission need causes A3's greeting-versus-admission division; B4's training assignment causes A5's staggered finger-and-wrist sequence.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs competence for the door job and B4 supplies an actual responsibility assigned by the president.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's new training authority to reproduce the measured hierarchy rather than grant full knowledge.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a first club-door shift and partial secret handshake.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's waiting-outside arrangement follows the parts withheld in A1-A3 and B4's next trainee.
